title: Preferences for Vital Pulp Treatments in Primary Molars: A Survey of Spanish Dentists.
abstract: Aim: To assess the preferences of dentists working in Spain regarding the management of deep caries removal and carious pulp exposures in primary molars. Methodology: An anonymous web-based survey was developed with Microsoft Forms (Microsoft Office 365) and distributed through social media among dentists in Spain. The questionnaire was divided into five sections regarding demographic data, caries removal management, pulp exposure decision-making, direct pulp capping and pulpotomy procedures. Likelihood ratio and logistic regression analyses were performed (p < 0.05). Results: A total of 228 valid responses were collected. Selective excavation to firm dentine was the preferred strategy for deep carious lesions (66.1%). Carious pulp exposure in vital asymptomatic primary molars was mainly managed with pulpotomy (48.3%) or direct pulp capping (48.7%). Pulpotomy was preferred for reversible pulpitis (66.7%), while pulpectomy was favoured for irreversible pulpitis (58.3%). Direct pulp capping was routinely performed by 42.2% and pulpotomy by 88.4% of respondents. These practices were significantly associated with the self-reported area of expertise and continuous education in vital pulp treatment. Haemostasis was most often achieved with a dry cotton pellet (direct pulp capping: 50.5%; pulpotomy: 47.7%). title: Innovative mHealth intervention providing sustained anticipatory guidance (zero cavity): Design, validation, user perception and effectiveness - A randomized controlled trial protocol.
abstract: Introduction: Early Childhood Caries (ECC) remains one of the most common chronic conditions in childhood, affecting over 600 million children globally. When untreated, it can lead to severe pain, abscesses, difficulty in chewing that contributes to malnutrition, impaired speech, disrupted sleep, low self-esteem, social withdrawal, and poor academic performance, all of which diminish a child's overall quality of life. Although largely preventable, ECC remains highly prevalent because of delayed preventive care and low parental awareness. Effective health education needs to be consistent, accessible, and available whenever parents need it. Although current evidence indicates that anticipatory guidance is a proven approach, its long-term reinforcement through a mobile app has not yet been tested. This study aims to develop and evaluate the effectiveness of a mobile health (mHealth) application delivering Sustained Anticipatory Guidance (SAG) for the prevention of ECC. Methods And Analysis: A two-arm parallel hospital-based randomized controlled trial will be conducted at Sri Ramachandra Institute of Higher Education & Research, Chennai, India. The study will enrol 540 mother-infant dyads from the departments of Pediatric Medicine and the Centre for Early Childhood Caries Research (CECCRe). title: Comparative Evaluation of NaOCl/EDTA-Based Multi-Step Protocol Versus Triton-Based Single-Step Protocol on Reduction of Bacterial DNA and RNA Levels: A Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial.
abstract: Objectives: Root canal irrigation plays a critical role in microbial reduction; however, culture-based methods may not fully detect residual microorganisms. This study compared the antibacterial efficacy of NaOCl/EDTA-based multi-step irrigation (MSIP) and Triton-based single-step irrigation (SSIP) protocols using molecular analysis. Methods: This double-blind study included 28 patients with maxillary central incisors diagnosed with pulp necrosis and asymptomatic apical periodontitis. Participants were randomized to group 1 (MSIP) and group 2 (SSIP) (n = 14 each). Bacterial samples were collected from the root canals before and after chemomechanical preparation (S1 and S2, respectively). All samples were placed in cryotubes containing RNAlater solution and transferred for molecular analysis. Data were analysed using Welch's t-test and two-way mixed-design repeated-measures ANOVA at p < 0.05. Results: The reduction from S1 to S2 was significantly greater with SSIP than with MSIP for both log10-transformed DNA and RNA. The mean between-group difference in reduction (SSIP - MSIP) was 0.259 log10 units for DNA (95% CI, 0.120-0.398; Holm-adjusted p = 0.0009) and 0.508 log10 units for RNA (95% CI, 0.334-0.681; Holm-adjusted p < 0.0002). Complementary mixed-design repeated-measures ANOVA demonstrated significant time × group interactions for both DNA (p = 0.0006) and RNA (p < 0.0001). title: Rotary First: A Technique for Simultaneous Root Canal Negotiation and Glide Path Establishment-An In Vitro Study.
abstract: Objectives: This preliminary in vitro study compared active instrumentation time and instrument fracture between the rotary first technique, which combines engine-driven canal negotiation and glide path establishment, and conventional manual instrumentation. Methods: Thirty freshly extracted human maxillary molars (103 canals) with canal curvatures ≤ 30° were randomised at tooth level to the rotary first or manual group. Active instrumentation time was compared separately in palatal (P), distobuccal (DB), mesiobuccal (MB) and second mesiobuccal (MB2) canals using 2-sided Mann-Whitney U-tests with Holm-Bonferroni adjustment. Overall canal-level fracture frequencies were compared exploratorily using a 2-sided Fisher's exact test. Results: Median active instrumentation time was lower with rotary first in every canal type. After multiplicity adjustment, the difference remained statistically significant only in MB canals (6.3 vs. 55.0 s; adjusted P = .004; rrb = 0.70). Differences in P (adjusted P = .087), DB (adjusted P = .100) and MB2 canals (adjusted P = .354) were not statistically significant. Fractures occurred in 7/53 rotary first canals (13.2%) and 2/50 manual canals (4.0%); the difference was not statistically significant (P = .162). title: Dual-phase deep learning recommendation system for radiographic crown lengthening assessment and post selection for the restoration of endodontically treated teeth.
abstract: Statement Of Problem: Restoring endodontically treated teeth requires careful evaluation of the supracrestal tissue attachment, ferrule integrity, and post-space dimensions to ensure long-term success. Manual radiographic analysis for crown lengthening indication and post selection is often time-consuming, subjective, and inconsistent, particularly in resource-limited settings where specialist access may be constrained. Purpose: The purpose of this study was to design and validate an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven system that automated 2 essential restorative planning tasks, evaluating the clinical need for crown lengthening and recommending appropriate post dimensions in endodontically treated teeth, using dental radiographs as the input. Material And Methods: Two deep learning pipelines were developed and trained on annotated panoramic and periapical datasets with annotations created under the supervision of dentistry professionals. The crown measurement pipeline employed a U-shaped network (U-Net) model for initial tooth segmentation (assigning unique instance masks to each tooth), then cropping individual teeth and feeding them into a Mask Region-based Convolutional Neural Network (Mask R-CNN) for precise detection and crown length calculation, facilitating the assessment of parameters such as supracrestal tissue attachment and ferrule height, for identification of potential violations or restoration limitations. title: A Comparative Benchmark of Modern Deep Learning Backbones for Multi-Class Periodontal Bone Loss Staging.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Early diagnosis of periodontal disease is critical to prevent tissue destruction and tooth loss. This study evaluates six modern deep learning architectures for four-class radiographic periodontal bone loss grading on panoramic radiographs. Methods: This retrospective study analyzed 1053 images. Two periodontologists independently classified each image according to the most severely affected tooth into four bone loss categories: Healthy, Mild (<25%), Moderate (25-50%), and Severe (>50%). Six convolutional, transformer, and hybrid backbones (ConvNeXt-Tiny, MaxViT-Tiny, EfficientViT-B1, FocalNet-Tiny, CAFormer-S18, and DaViT-Tiny) were trained on a 70/10/20 stratified split using an NVIDIA Tesla T4 GPU, the AdamW optimizer, Cosine Annealing, and early stopping. Performance was assessed using standard classification metrics, Matthews Correlation Coefficient, Cohen's and Quadratic Weighted Kappa, Expected Calibration Error, Area Under the Curve (AUC), McNemar's test, and bootstrap 95% confidence intervals. Results: FocalNet-Tiny achieved the highest numerical scores among the tested models, reaching 83.41% accuracy, 84.70% balanced accuracy, 83.50% macro-F1, and 0.9610 OvR AUC. title: Machine Learning Prediction of Orthodontic Extraction Patterns Using Multimodal Features Derived From Intraoral Scans and Lateral Cephalometric Radiographs.
abstract: Objective: To develop and evaluate a machine learning framework for predicting orthodontic extraction patterns using features extracted from pretreatment intraoral scans (IOS) and lateral cephalometric radiographs (LCRs). Materials And Methods: This retrospective study included 420 subjects (mean age, 17.1 years; 61% female) with treatment plans involving dental extractions. Expert consensus-derived reference labels were established using a validated Delphi process involving four orthodontic experts. The dataset was randomly split into two mutually exclusive subsets: 30% for hyperparameter optimization using grid search with five-fold cross-validation and 70% (n = 294) for model development and evaluation using leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV). Performance was assessed using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values, likelihood ratios and F1 score. Results: The Gradient Boosting classifier trained exclusively on canine-molar relationship features achieved the highest overall classification accuracy (79.9%), whereas the Random Forest multimodal model incorporating all IOS- and LCR-derived features achieved 78.2% accuracy and did not provide a significant improvement over canine-molar relationship features alone. SHAP analysis identified canine and molar relationships as the most influential predictors. For the Random Forest multimodal model, class-specific sensitivity (recall) was 84% for Class I, 77% for Class II, and 48% for Class III.

title: Conservative Management of a Type IIIA Dens Invaginatus -A Case Report.
abstract: To describe the conservative management of a type IIIA dens invaginatus (DI) aiming to preserve pulp vitality. A 13-year-old male patient presented with recurrent episodes of swelling and pain associated with tooth 22. Clinical examination revealed an intact tooth with a positive response to cold sensibility testing. Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) confirmed the presence of a type IIIA DI associated with a lateral radiolucent lesion adjacent to the communication between the invagination and the periodontal ligament, while the apical region remained intact. A conservative treatment approach restricted to the invagination was planned using CBCT virtual reconstruction to preserve pulp vitality. After rubber dam isolation and access under dental operating microscope magnification, the invagination was prepared using a Reciproc R25 instrument and irrigated with 2.5% sodium hypochlorite and 17% ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid. Calcium hydroxide paste was used as intracanal medication for 30 days with replacement after 15 days. The invagination was obturated using the single-cone technique with gutta-percha and a bioceramic sealer, followed by composite resin restoration. title: Geminated Maxillary Incisors With Talon Cusp: A Case Report With Management and Narrative Review.
abstract: Background And Objectives: Recognition of teeth with gemination and/or talon cusp, along with early treatment, is important to prevent complications such as occlusal interference, malocclusion, the formation of caries and periodontal pockets, and esthetic issues. This case report is aimed at describing the multidisciplinary management of a rare case of geminated permanent maxillary central incisors associated with a talon cusp and to review similar cases previously reported in the literature. Materials And Methods: The diagnoses were determined through a combination of intraoral photographs, dental casts, periapical x-rays, and cone-beam computed tomography. A long-term, multidisciplinary treatment plan was developed for managing this geminated tooth with a talon cusp. Results: This case report describes the successful diagnosis and management of an 11-year-old patient with Class II malocclusion and bilateral gemination of the two maxillary incisors. A unilateral talon cusp was erupting on the palatal surface of the malpositioned maxillary left central incisor, extending from the cervical area toward the incisal edge and reaching approximately two-thirds of the crown length. The talon cusp caused occlusal interference with the mandibular left lateral incisor, and a 5-mm periodontal pocket had formed at the distopalatal site of the maxillary left central incisor. title: Concentrated Growth Factor and Non-Cross-Linked Collagen Fleece Improve Palatal Donor-Site Healing and Reduce Post-Operative Morbidity: A Randomised Controlled Clinical Trial.
abstract: Aim: To compare the effects of stabilised concentrated growth factor (CGF) and collagen fleece (CF) on palatal donor-site healing, tissue thickness, pain and quality of life. Materials And Methods: Thirty-nine patients undergoing standardised palatal graft harvesting were randomised to CGF, CF or control (gelatine sponge) groups (n = 13 per group), of whom 38 completed the study. All materials were sutured and sealed with oral dressing and tissue adhesive. Palatal soft-tissue thickness (PSTT), modified Manchester scar scale (MSS), wound area, visual analogue scale (VAS), analgesic intake and Oral Health Impact Profile-14 (OHIP-14) were evaluated over 6 months. Results: The CGF group showed greater PSTT at 3 months than the control, and the CF group showed greater PSTT at 1 and 3 months versus baseline (p < 0.05). Both test groups demonstrated faster MSS normalisation (p < 0.05), smaller wound areas at Days 7 and 14 (p < 0.01), lower VAS scores during Days 0-6 (p < 0.05) and greater OHIP-14 improvements at Day 3 (p < 0.001). Analgesic use during Days 4-7 was lower in the CGF group (p = 0.013). Conclusions: Within the limits of this study, both CGF and CF appeared to enhance early palatal donor-site healing and reduce postoperative morbidity, with faster epithelialisation, smaller wound areas and improved patient-reported outcomes.

title: Clinical indications and conditions of third-molar germectomy and early adolescent extractions: a retrospective analysis.
abstract: Objectives: This retrospective study evaluated third-molar (M3) germectomy/early adolescent extractions, focusing on clinical and radiographic characteristics, removal indications, and possible effects on adjacent second molars (M2s). Methods: Records of 112 adolescent patients (mean age, 16.10 ± 0.92 years; range, 12.92-17.00 years) who underwent M3 germectomy/early adolescent M3 extraction between 2017 and 2023 were reviewed. A total of 234 M3s were assessed on panoramic radiographs using established radiographic classification systems for positional, angulation, and developmental evaluation. Removal indications and M2 pathology, positional changes, and treatment needs were recorded. Statistical analyses included chi-square tests, multivariable logistic regression, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, with significance set at p < 0.05. Results: Among the 234 M3s, 73 (31.2%) had Demirjian stages C-E (germectomy subgroup), whereas 161 (68.8%) had stages F-H (early adolescent extraction subgroup). The leading removal indications were orthodontic space management (37.2%) and pericoronitis (34.2%). Jaw-based differences were largest for removal indication (Cramér's V = 0.65) and Winter angulation (V = 0.52), followed by Archer position (V = 0.48) and Demirjian stage (V = 0.35). title: Sleep Deprivation Exacerbates Pulpal Inflammation and Impairs Repair Through Dysregulated Neutrophil Activity in Rats.
abstract: Aim: To investigate the effects of sleep deprivation on pulpal inflammation and repair and determine the contribution of neutrophil activity to these changes in rat models. Methodology: Sleep deprivation was induced in rats using a modified multiple platform method. Pulp responses were evaluated using three experimental settings. Under baseline conditions, rats underwent acute sleep deprivation for four consecutive days. In the inflammatory model, pulpitis was induced by lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and assessed 1-4 days after induction. In the reparative model, direct pulp capping (DPC) was performed and pulpal healing was assessed at 14 and 28 days during sleep deprivation. Histological, vascular and inflammatory changes were evaluated by haematoxylin and eosin staining, Masson's trichrome staining, immunohistochemistry and immunofluorescence. Transcriptomic alterations in pulp tissue were analysed by mRNA sequencing. Neutrophil abundance and activation were assessed in peripheral blood and dental pulp by complete blood counts, flow cytometry and myeloperoxidase staining. To investigate the functional contribution of neutrophils and neutrophil elastase (NE), sleep-deprived rats were treated with the neutrophil-depleting antibody or the NE inhibitor Sivelestat. title: Static, Dynamic and Robotic CAIS in Healed Partially Edentulous Sites: Accuracy and Chair-Side Time.
journal: Clinical implant dentistry and related research
abstract: Aim: To evaluate the accuracy and chair-side efficiency of static (s-CAIS), dynamic (d-CAIS), and autonomous robotic (r-CAIS) computer-assisted implant surgery in healed partially edentulous sites. Materials And Methods: In this retrospective comparative study, 73 patients with 92 implants, treated from September 2022 to October 2024, were included (s-CAIS: 21 patients/33 implants; d-CAIS: 29 patients/32 implants; r-CAIS: 23 patients/27 implants). Pre- and postoperative CBCT scans were used to assess linear and angular deviations. The duration of chair-side preparation and drilling/implant placement was recorded for d-CAIS and r-CAIS. Results: At implant level, mean platform deviations were 0.85 ± 0.38 mm (s-CAIS), 1.37 ± 0.71 mm (d-CAIS), and 0.59 ± 0.32 mm (r-CAIS; median [IQR]: 0.54 [0.30] mm); apex deviations were 1.36 ± 0.51, 1.48 ± 0.66, and 0.64 ± 0.52 mm (r-CAIS; median [IQR]: 0.53 [0.30] mm); angular deviations were 4.34° ± 2.13°, 2.53° ± 0.99°, and 1.54° ± 1.50° (r-CAIS; median [IQR]: 1.28° [1.40°]). title: [The molar uprighting device: A conservative approach to the orthodontic management of mesially tipped and submucosal molars].
abstract: Introduction: Eruption anomalies of permanent molars, particularly mesial inclinations that cause mechanical impaction, represent a common clinical challenge in orthodontics. Traditionally, the lack of coronal access and the difficulties associated with traction have led to routine extractions, compromising tooth preservation and the possibility of achieving a functional occlusion comprising at least 28 teeth. The molar uprighting device offers a conservative alternative based on the use of a heat-activated 0.014-inch nickel-titanium wire (shape memory effect heat-activated NiTi), inserted into the interproximal space and then bonded to the adjacent tooth, which serves as anchorage. Thanks to its superelasticity, the wire delivers gentle, continuous force, generating distal tipping movement that enables gradual uprighting of the mesially tipped molar without direct access to its crown. Materials And Method: Ten patients presenting with a mesially tipped molar impacted against the adjacent tooth, with no communication with the oral cavity, were included in this study. A 0.014-inch-diameter heat-activated shape-memory nickel-titanium (NiTi) wire was inserted vertically into the interproximal space between the two teeth, then bent over and bonded to the occlusal surface of the anterior tooth already in occlusion. Results: The clinical results presented demonstrate reproducible uprighting, predictable vertical positioning, and functional eruption, with no iatrogenic complications

title: Combined Nonsurgical Endodontic Treatment and Palatal Endodontic Microsurgery for Oehlers Type IIIa Dens Invaginatus: A Case Report.
abstract: Dens invaginatus (DI) is an uncommon developmental dental anomaly. In complex cases, its aberrant anatomy, often combined with pulpal infection and periapical disease, presents substantial therapeutic challenges. This report describes a case of Oehlers type IIIa DI associated with chronic apical periodontitis in a maxillary lateral incisor. The patient presented with recurrent suppuration and pain in the maxillary anterior region. Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) revealed a typical type IIIa DI in tooth 22, accompanied by extensive periapical bone destruction involving both teeth 21 and 22. Following a comprehensive evaluation, both teeth underwent nonsurgical root canal treatment, fibre-reinforced splinting, and palatal endodontic microsurgery. Follow-up examinations at 3, 10, 16 and 28 months demonstrated complete resolution of clinical symptoms and favourable radiographic healing, with progressive reduction of the periapical radiolucency and new bone formation. This case suggests that a combination of nonsurgical endodontic treatment and palatal endodontic microsurgery, guided by detailed CBCT assessment, may be considered in carefully selected cases of Oehlers type IIIa DI with extensive periapical lesions. The favourable outcome observed in this patient adds to the limited literature on tooth-preserving management of complex type IIIa DI.

title: Effectiveness of Dog-Assisted Support to Promote Compliance and Home Oral Hygiene Activities in Disabled Patients: A Randomised Clinical Trial.
abstract: Objective: Dental anxiety is a negative emotional reaction that can have a negative impact on oral health. Structured animal-assisted services (AAS) involve trained dogs to promote positive behaviours during treatments that may otherwise cause anxiety in the patient. It has been proved that AAS used even for a short time can significantly reduce stress markers. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness of home oral hygiene using AAS in patients with disabilities. Methods: The study was a randomised clinical trial. The participants were randomised into two groups. In group A the oral hygiene session was performed with the presence of a trained therapy dog; in group B it was carried out in a regular dental setup. Patients included in the study were between 5 and 16 years old; disabled; non-collaborating or with limited collaboration; with scarce oral hygiene. Plaque control record (PCR) pre, post oral hygiene procedures, and the patient's feelings were recorded. Results: Eighty patients were included in the study. Comparison of PCR at T1 between groups shows a statistically significant difference (p < 0.001) with a higher decrease in this index for patients in group A. Regarding the emotional state of patients, the statistical test shows a higher frequency (p = 0.002) of responses 'happy,' 'interested,' and 'calm' in the group of patients who performed the oral hygiene procedures with the assistance of dogs. title: Prevalence and Associated Risk Factors for Xerostomia in a Group of Patients With Arthritis.
journal: Special care in dentistry : official publication of the American Association of Hospital Dentists, the Academy of Dentistry for the Handicapped, and the American Society for Geriatric Dentistry
abstract: Background: Xerostomia is commonly reported among patients with rheumatological diseases. Evidence on its prevalence and associated factors across types of arthritis remains limited. Methods And Results: A cross-sectional observational study was conducted among members of ConArtritis (Spanish National Coordinator of Arthritis Patient Associations). Patients with rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, or juvenile idiopathic arthritis were recruited (October 2024-January 2025). An online questionnaire collected sociodemographic data, lifestyle habits, comorbidities, and medications. Xerostomia was assessed with a validated screening question, and its severity was measured with the Xerostomia Inventory (XI). OHRQoL was evaluated using the OHIP-14. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed. Among 108 participants (88% women; mean age 50.6 years), 84.3% reported xerostomia and 19.4% had a previous Sjögren's disease diagnosis. Patients with xerostomia were older. XI and OHIP-14 scores were higher in xerostomic patients, with a strong positive XI-OHIP-14 correlation. Multivariate analysis identified older age and low back pain as factors associated with xerostomia. Conclusion: Xerostomia was highly prevalent in this sample of patients with arthritis and is linked to older age, selected comorbidities, and poorer OHRQoL. title: Oral Health Knowledge, Practice, and Oral Health Status among Garment Employees of Bangladesh: A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: Background And Aims: Oral health remain an overlooked component of workers' well-being in low-income settings, particularly in labour-intensive industries such as Bangladesh's ready-made garment (RMG) sector. So, the major aim of this study was to assess the oral health knowledge, practices, and self-reported oral health status among Bangladeshi garment employees. Methods: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 502 garment workers from Gazipur district between May and December 2024. Data on oral health knowledge, hygiene practices, and self-reported symptoms were collected using a validated questionnaire. Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and logistic regression analyses were performed. Results: Although 76.5% (384/502) of participants demonstrated good oral health knowledge, 29.3% (147/502) reported a need for dental care. Healthy oral hygiene practices were highly prevalent (493/502, 98.2%), yet knowledge, age, marital status, and education were significantly associated with oral health outcomes (p < 0.05). Workers experiencing dental pain within the previous 12 months were 58.9 times more likely to seek treatment (AOR = 58.89; 95% CI: 32.90-105.41). Conclusion: This study highlights a critical gap between knowledge and actual oral health needs among garment workers. The findings underscore the need for workplace-based oral health education, affordable dental services, and integration of oral care into occupational health policies.

title: Biochemical and gasometric profiles of mandibular and Iliac bone marrow compared with peripheral blood: implications for bone regeneration.
abstract: Purpose: To compare biochemical characteristics of blood samples obtained from different anatomical sites: mandibular bone marrow, iliac bone marrow, and peripheral blood. Methods: This study included 26 patients undergoing dental implant placement and maxillary reconstruction with iliac bone grafting. Blood samples were collected from mandibular bone marrow, iliac bone marrow, and peripheral venous blood. Gasometric analysis evaluated PCO₂, PO₂, TCO₂, oxygen saturation (SatO₂), ionized calcium, pH, lactate, and magnesium. Statistical analysis included the Shapiro-Wilk test, repeated measures ANOVA with Bonferroni post hoc, and the Friedman test with Wilcoxon comparisons (p < 0.05). Results: Mandibular bone marrow blood showed significantly higher pH, PO₂, and oxygen saturation, and lower PCO₂ and HCO₃⁻ compared to other sites. These findings indicate a more oxygenated and less acidic microenvironment. No significant differences were observed for lactate, magnesium, and ionized calcium. Conclusion: Mandibular bone marrow exhibits a more favorable biochemical profile for osteogenic metabolism, suggesting its potential advantage for bone graft integration and autologous blood derivatives. The study was published in the Brazilian Registry of Clinical Trials (ReBEC) under number RBR-5mwjh3z, on 4 July 2026, retrospectively registered.

title: Radiographic Quality and Periapical Status of Post-Retained Restorations: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: Introduction And Aims: Contemporary data evaluating endodontic, post, coronal and practice-setting parameters of post-retained restorations together in a multivariable framework remain limited. This multicentre retrospective cross-sectional study evaluated the radiographic technical quality and current periapical status of post-retained restorations and identified factors associated with them. Methods: Periapical radiographs of 459 post-retained restorations from 366 patients were assessed across three clinical settings in Jordan (February 2020 to December 2025). Post dimensions and angulation, remaining gutta-percha (RGP), root canal filling length and density, post and coronal marginal adaptation, secondary caries and periapical status (periapical index [PAI]) were recorded. Restorations were graded on a study-specific composite scale and dichotomised into satisfactory (Grades 1-2) and unsatisfactory (Grade 3). Associations were modelled using generalised estimating equations (GEEs) clustered by patient, reporting adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results: Technical quality was satisfactory in 45.8% of restorations (95% CI: 41.2%-50.3%) and periapical radiolucency (PAR) was present in 31.6% (27.5%-36.0%). title: Interceptive Management of Ectopically Erupting Maxillary Canines With Rapid Maxillary Expansion and Clear Aligners: A Case Report.
abstract: Objective: Maxillary canine impaction represents one of the most common eruption disturbances in orthodontics after third molars. This case report describes the management of a 9.2-year-old growing male patient with bilateral ectopic eruption of the maxillary permanent canines, transverse maxillary deficiency, mesiorotation of the upper first molars, and bilateral Class II molar relationship. The patient was treated according to the BIG-C concept (Biomechanical Interceptive Guidance of Canine Eruption)-a biomechanically guided interceptive approach combining rapid maxillary expansion, sequential distalization with clear aligners, and arch-perimeter management. Methods: Radiographic changes were assessed on serial panoramic radiographs using the Ericson and Kurol criteria, including α-angle and sector classification at baseline (T0), after RME (T1), and after sequential distalization (T2). Clinical and radiographic follow-up was continued until eruption and progressive alignment of both permanent canines following interceptive treatment were observed (T3). Results: Both maxillary canines showed progressive radiographic improvement. The α-angle decreased from 44.5° to 17.7° for Tooth 1.3 and from 47.1° to 18.7° for Tooth 2.3, corresponding to total reductions of 60.2% and 60.3%, respectively. title: [Impact of mini-screws inserted in the maxilla and mandible, adjacent to extraction sites or agenetic teeth, on alveolar bone gain or loss].
abstract: Introduction: In dentistry, it is now commonly accepted that the absence or even the loss of the dental organ inevitably leads to alveolar bone atrophy. The latter resorbs in height then in width, continuously, and nothing can go against this physiological phenomenon. The hypothesis that a mini-screw could maintain the alveolar bone and prevent and/or reduce its atrophy is validated on the growing canine and porcine model. Objective: The objective of this study is to evaluate the impact of mini-screws inserted in the maxilla and the mandible, nearby edentulous ridges, on the final bone volume surrounding them. Materials And Method: This study is interventional, prospective, and non-randomized, conducted on 64 patients (32 males and 32 females) requiring orthodontic management, aged between 12 and 19 years, for which 104 mini-screws were inserted next to toothless spaces. In order to evaluate the behavior of the edentulous sites in height and width, intraoral photographs, dental impressions, and cone beam radiological examinations were carried out at T0 (before insertion of the TADs) and at T1 (one year after their insertion). For all comparisons, we used a significance level of 5%, and the estimates were expressed with a confidence interval of 95%. title: Influence of non-surgical periodontal therapy on inflammasome biomarkers in periodontitis with and without diabetes mellitus.
abstract: Background: Periodontitis and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are chronic inflammatory conditions linked through common pathogenic processes. Interleukin-18 (IL-18), absent in melanoma 2 (AIM2), and interferon gamma-inducible protein 16 (IFI16) have been associated with inflammatory pathways of both diseases. Limited data exist regarding the effect of non-surgical periodontal therapy (NSPT) on these biomarkers. This study was designed to evaluate and compare the effect of NSPT on serum levels of AIM2, IFI16, and IL-18 in stage III periodontitis patients with and without T2DM. Methods: Ninety participants were allocated into three groups: periodontally healthy controls (group I), stage III periodontitis (group II), stage III periodontitis with T2DM (group III). The plaque index (PI), gingival index (GI), papillary bleeding index (PBI), probing pocket depth (PPD), clinical attachment level (CAL), gingival recession (GR), periodontal inflamed surface area (PISA), periodontal epithelial surface area (PESA), random blood sugar (RBS), HbA1c, AIM2, IFI16, and IL-18 were assessed at baseline in group I and also at 6 weeks in groups II and III. Results: Serum AIM2, IFI16, and IL-18 levels were significantly elevated in periodontitis patients, with the highest concentrations observed in group III, followed by group II at baseline. title: Forecasting endodontic outcomes from intraoral radiographs using a deep convolutional neural network.
abstract: This study aimed to develop and evaluate a generalized deep convolutional neural network (DCNN) model, ApexNet-17, for predicting endodontic outcomes across all tooth types using preoperative periapical radiographs. A dataset comprising 2,603 teeth from two institutions was utilized. Endodontic outcomes were determined based on tooth survival and radiographic periapical health during 1-3 years of follow-up using the periapical index (PAI). A 17-layer DCNN incorporating self-attention, attention pooling, and five radiographic features was trained and internally validated using 2,279 cases and externally tested using 324 cases. Gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) was applied to visualize regions contributing to model predictions. ApexNet-17 achieved an accuracy of 72.1%, a sensitivity of 58.5%, and an AUC of 0.666-performance that, while improved over the pilot model, remains below the level typically considered acceptable for clinical decision support. Compared with the previous premolar-only model, ApexNet-17 showed statistically higher accuracy and sensitivity (p < 0.05) but substantially lower specificity (50.6% vs. 78.3%), indicating a higher false-positive rate. Because the models were evaluated using different datasets, these comparisons should be interpreted cautiously, and statistical significance should not be regarded as evidence of clinical superiority. title: Masticatory Function in Patients With Oligodontia: A Systematic Review of Baseline Impairments and Post-Rehabilitative Outcomes.
abstract: Objectives: To synthesize evidence on baseline masticatory impairment and post-rehabilitation outcomes in patients with oligodontia. Methods: This systematic review followed PRISMA 2020 and was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251090932). PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase and Cochrane were searched to August 2026. The included populations comprised patients with syndromic and non-syndromic oligodontia. The main outcomes included direct and indirect objective assessments of masticatory function, patient-reported chewing and eating function, and broader oral health-related quality-of-life outcomes. Risk of bias was assessed using design-specific JBI tools and ROBINS-I, and certainty of evidence using GRADE. Results: Thirteen studies were included, with evidence derived predominantly from small observational studies and substantial heterogeneity in age, syndromic status, rehabilitation modality and outcome assessment. Baseline evidence indicated eating- and chewing-related functional burden, but the evidence for patient-reported and broader functional impairment was of very low certainty, and untreated objective masticatory impairment could not be reliably quantified. title: Dietary Intake Associated with Periodontitis in Adults: A Scoping Review.
abstract: Background: Periodontitis continues to be a global public health burden that is associated with an increased risk of metabolic diseases such as type 2 diabetes mellitus, metabolic syndrome, and cardiovascular diseases. Several studies, unsystematized, have evaluated the relationship between consumption of specific foods, nutrients, or eating patterns and the disease, aiming to support personalized and holistic periodontal therapy. Objective: This scoping review aimed to evaluate which dietary intakes are linked to the pathology. Methods: The scoping review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines. A systematic search was conducted in PubMed. The inclusion criteria were original studies with adult populations that evaluated diet and nutrient intake in populations with periodontitis. Results: Thirty-six articles were included (26 cross-sectional, 6 cohort studies, 3 randomized clinical trials, and 1 case-control). Specifically, adequate protein intake significantly reduced bleeding on probing, while high fiber intake was inversely associated with alveolar bone loss and tooth loss. Furthermore, higher consumption of vitamins C and D correlated with a reduced periodontitis risk. title: Immediate Implant Placement With Peri-Implant Contour Augmentation in the Maxillary Central Incisor: A Three-Year Clinical and Cone-Beam Computed Tomography Follow-Up.
abstract: Although immediate implant placement in the anterior maxilla can shorten the treatment timeline, it presents challenges in preserving peri-implant hard- and soft-tissue contours. We report the three-year clinical and radiographic outcome of immediate implant placement combined with peri-implant contour augmentation in the region of the maxillary right central incisor. A 20-year-old man presented two months after trauma with a non-restorable cervical fracture of the maxillary right central incisor. Clinical and cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) evaluation demonstrated facial bone deficiency with sufficient apical and palatal bone for immediate implant placement. Following atraumatic extraction, a 4 × 14 mm implant was placed in a prosthetically driven three-dimensional position with primary stability of 35 Ncm. The peri-implant gap and facial contour were augmented using deproteinized bovine bone mineral (Bio-Oss®, Geistlich Pharma AG, Wolhusen, Switzerland) and a resorbable collagen membrane. Following uneventful healing, second-stage surgery was performed at three months, followed by definitive ceramic crown placement. At the three-year follow-up, the implant remained clinically stable, with healthy peri-implant soft tissues and preserved facial contour, without signs of inflammation, infection, or mobility. title: Cognitive Evaluation of Multimodal Large Language Models in Dental Radiography.
abstract: Objectives: We evaluated the cognitive capabilities and safety boundaries of general-purpose, zero-shot multimodal large language models (MLLMs) in dental radiography. Methods: OralMLLM-Bench comprised 27 independently evaluated tasks across periapical, panoramic, and lateral cephalometric radiographs, grouped into four categories: perception, comprehension, prediction, and decision-making. Six MLLMs and two clinician comparators were evaluated across 3,820 assessment units using sensitivity, specificity, balanced accuracy (BA), partial-credit average score (PCAS), and conditional rationale accuracy (CRA). Results: MLLMs showed relatively stronger performance for selected visually salient findings, with sensitivity up to 0.917 for root filling detection and 0.875 for restoration detection, but lower performance for low-contrast findings and spatial localization. Only 6 of 27 tasks showed significant between-model differences after false discovery rate correction, with no broad, consistent advantage for any model. Agreement with expert image-based reference assessments was generally limited in prediction and decision-making tasks. title: Comparison of laterally closed tunnel and free gingival graft for isolated anterior mandibular recessions: a randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Objectives: To compare the laterally closed tunnel (LCT) technique combined with connective tissue graft (CTG) and free gingival graft (FGG) in the treatment of isolated gingival recessions in the anterior mandibular region. Materials And Methods: Twenty-one patients were divided into two groups: the LCT group (n = 10), treated using the LCT technique with CTG; and the FGG group (n = 11), treated using FGG. Periodontal clinical parameters were evaluated at baseline and after 1, 3, 6, and 12 months. The Landry index, root coverage esthetic score, and visual analog scale for pain were also evaluated. Statistical modeling was used to assess the impact of treatment and clinical factors on 12-month root coverage, with scenario-based predictions supporting personalized planning. Results: A progressive improvement in root coverage and keratinized tissue thickness was observed in both groups, although no significant differences were found. Greater keratinized tissue height was observed in the FGG group at all follow-up periods (p < 0.05). title: Electrical stimulation of adipose-derived stem cells encapsulated in an electrically conductive hydrogel promotes wound healing and osteogenesis.
abstract: Background: Periodontitis is a common oral disease with global health concerns, and the healing process involves mucosal recovery and osteogenesis. The aim of this study was to develop an electrical stimulation (ES)-on-stem cell (ES-SC) strategy for facilitating wound healing and promoting osteogenesis, which serve as critical prerequisites for periodontal regeneration, and adipose-derived stem cells (ADSCs) were utilized as the source of stem cells. Human ADSCs (hADSCs) were isolated, and their cell viability and osteogenicity in culture dishes and in ECH under ES were examined in vitro. Rat ADSCs (rADSCs) were isolated, and the preclinical feasibility of ES on rADSC-laden GelMA/PEDOT: PSS was subsequently assessed using a rat wound healing model and an osteogenesis model to simulate soft tissue repair and osteogenesis, respectively. Results: Under ES, hADSCs were aligned with enhanced osteogenicity. title: Antibacterial, anti-biofilm, and depth-penetrant activity of a Cissus quadrangularis mediated biogenic Ag-HAp-MSN nanocomposite against cariogenic pathogens.
abstract: Cariogenic biofilms primarily associated with Streptococcus mutans and Lactobacillus acidophilus contribute to one of the most prevalent chronic oral diseases worldwide. Although current Casein Phosphopeptide-Amorphous Calcium Phosphate (CPP-ACP) systems are effective in remineralization, they lack direct biofilm-disrupting capabilities, highlighting the need for multifunctional materials. A biogenic Ag-HAp-MSN nanocomposite, previously synthesized using Cissus quadrangularis extract and confirmed to possess favourable physicochemical properties and cytocompatibility, was evaluated for its antibacterial and anti-biofilm efficacy. Antibacterial activity was assessed using agar well diffusion, Minimum Inhibitory Concentration (MIC), and Minimum Bactericidal Concentration (MBC) assays, while anti-biofilm activity was analysed via crystal violet inhibition, acridine orange/ethidium bromide (AO/EB) live-dead fluorescence, and Confocal Laser Scanning Microscopy (CLSM). title: Prevalence and factors associated with early childhood caries among three-year-old children attending child welfare clinics in Kalutara District, Sri Lanka: a cross-sectional study.
abstract: Background: Early childhood caries (ECC) remains a significant public health challenge in Sri Lanka, despite established preventive programs. Evidence on socio-behavioural and child-related factors associated with ECC among three-year-old children, particularly at the district level, is limited. This study assessed the prevalence of ECC and socio-behavioural and child-related factors associated with ECC among three-year-old children attending child welfare clinics (CWCs) in Kalutara District, Sri Lanka. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional study involving 1,197 mother-child dyads attending CWCs in the Kalutara District from May to September 2025, following the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) guidelines. Children aged three years (completed third but not fourth birthday) were included using multistage cluster sampling with probability proportional to size (PPS). Data on sociodemographics, dietary habits, and oral health behaviours were collected using a pre-tested, expert-validated, interviewer-administered questionnaire. Dental examinations were performed by a calibrated examiner using World Health Organization (WHO) criteria. Multivariable logistic regression identified variables independently associated with ECC (dmft ≥ 1). title: Comparison of apical microleakage between CEM cement and cold ceramic as root-end filling materials, an in vitro study.
abstract: Background: Public attitudes toward oral health have shifted toward preserving natural tooth structure. Achieving an effective apical seal is critical to prevent bacterial microleakage. This in vitro study aimed to compare apical microleakage between Calcium-Enriched Mixture (CEM) Cement and Cold Ceramic as root-end filling materials. Methods: Sixty extracted single-rooted human teeth with closed apices were used. After decoronation and root canal preparation, a 3-mm apical resection was performed, and 3-mm retrograde cavities were prepared using an ultrasonic device under magnification. Teeth were randomly assigned to two experimental groups (n = 25 each) receiving either CEM Cement (BioniqueDent) or Cold Ceramic (SANIN), plus positive and negative controls (n = 5 each). Bacterial leakage was assessed using a dual-chamber model with Enterococcus faecalis over 90 days. Statistical analysis included Fisher's exact test, Mann-Whitney U test, and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis. Results: Apical microleakage occurred in 72% of the CEM Cement group and 92% of the Cold Ceramic group. The difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.138). Mean time to leakage was 13.83 days (median 11.5 days) for CEM Cement and 12.70 days (median 10 days) for Cold Ceramic (p = 0.793). title: Consensus-Based Recommendations for the Management of Deep and Extremely Deep Carious Lesions and Vital Pulp Treatment in Permanent Teeth: A National Delphi Study.
abstract: Aim: To develop consensus-based recommendations for general dental practitioners on deep and extremely deep carious lesions (CLs) and vital pulp treatment (VPT) in mature and immature permanent teeth. Methodology: A national modified Delphi study was conducted with a purposively selected expert panel. Twenty-nine statements developed from international guidance were assessed through three anonymous online rounds using a 10-point agreement scale. Free-text justification for scores below 7 informed revision or merging. Positive consensus was predefined as a median score ≥ 7 with an interquartile range (IQR) ≤ 2; statements with greater dispersion could also be accepted when > 90% of experts scored them ≥ 7. Statements remaining uncertain after Round 3 were discussed at an online meeting and anonymously re-rated by the full panel. Results: Of 34 experts invited, 22 enrolled and completed every rating stage; no item-level data were missing. Five statements reached consensus in Round 1, 10 in Round 2, and six in Round 3. Four merging procedures reduced the 29 initial statements to 24 final statements. The remaining three reached consensus after the meeting and post-meeting rating; none was rejected. Final median scores ranged from 7 to 10, IQRs from 0 to 2, and proportions of scores ≥ 7 from 59.1% to 100%. title: Laser-assisted Excision Versus Conventional Scalpel Surgery in the Treatment of Benign Oral Soft-tissue Lesions.
abstract: Introduction: Laser-assisted excision of benign oral soft-tissue lesions is gaining recognition as an alternative and less invasive method. The purpose of this paper was to determine the efficacy of diode laser-assisted excision over conventional scalpel surgery in managing benign oral soft-tissue lesions. Materials And Methods: It was a prospective comparative clinical trial with 1800 patients who were randomized into two groups of equal size. The laser group had an excision with a 980 nm diode laser, whereas the conventional group was treated with scalpel excision. The clinical outcomes measured were the duration of the operation, blood loss during surgery, need for suturing, pain after surgery (visual analog scale), healing of the wound, side effects, recurrence, and satisfaction of the patients. Results: Laser-assisted excision significantly reduced operative time, bleeding scores, and suturing needs (P < 0.001). Postoperative pain and healing indices were superior in the laser group, with higher patient satisfaction and lower infection, scarring, and recurrence rates compared to scalpel surgery. Conclusion: Laser-assisted excision demonstrated clear advantages over conventional scalpel surgery, providing enhanced efficiency, reduced morbidity, and improved patient-centered outcomes.

title: Vital pulp therapy or root canal treatment? A 12-month clinical evaluation following prosthetic pulp exposure: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Background: This study retrospectively evaluated and compared the clinical and radiographic outcomes of full pulpotomy (FP) and root canal treatment (RCT) in teeth with iatrogenic pulp exposure during prosthetic crown preparation. Methods: Seventy-seven anterior and premolar teeth from 62 patients treated between October 2022 and October 2023 were included. All cases involved vital teeth without deep caries, treated within 24 h of pulpal exposure. FP was performed using Biodentine, whereas RCT followed a standardized crown-down protocol. Data on pain scores (VAS), analgesic use, treatment duration, and patient satisfaction were retrospectively extracted from standardized clinical records. Outcomes included recorded patient- and clinician-reported measures and radiographic evaluation using the periapical index (PAI). Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS v22.0 (SPSS Inc., Chicago, IL, USA). Categorical data were analyzed using Chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, and Mann-Whitney U and Spearman correlation tests for continuous variables (p < 0.05). Results: At the 12-month follow-up, clinical and radiographic success was 100% for FP and 93% for RCT (p = 0.328). FP showed significantly lower postoperative pain at 6, 12, 24, and 48 h (p < 0.05) and lower analgesic use (p = 0.001). title: CBCT features of florid cemento-osseous dysplasia with coexisting lesions at different maturation stages: a case report and literature review.
abstract: Background: Florid cemento-osseous dysplasia (FLCOD) is a begin fibro-osseous lesion occurring in the tooth-bearing regions of the jaws and is characterized by replacement of normal bone with fibrous connective tissue and cementum-like mineralized material. Most patients are asymptomatic and are diagnosed incidentally during radiographic examinations, and the condition may be misdiagnosed because of overlapping imaging features with other jaw lesions. Because the disease is usually asymptomatic and exhibits imaging features that overlap with those of several odontogenic and inflammatory lesions, accurate diagnosis remains challenging. Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) provides high-resolution three-dimensional imaging that facilitates assessment of lesion extent, internal mineralization, and relationships with adjacent anatomical structures. We report a case of FLCOD exhibiting lesions at different maturation stages and emphasize the diagnostic value of CBCT in clinical decision-making. Case Presentation: A 41-year-old female presented with pain in the left mandibular posterior region for one week. Clinical examination revealed deep carious destruction of tooth 36 and occlusal caries involving teeth 46 and 47. title: Comparative analysis of endodontic microbiota in apical root thirds using cryopulverization and paper point sampling techniques: a pilot exploratory next generation sequencing study.
abstract: Objectives: This study aimed to compare the effectiveness of paper point (PP) and cryopulverization (CP) microbial sampling techniques for characterizing the bacterial communities in the apical third of teeth with post-treatment apical periodontitis using 16 S rDNA sequencing. Amplicon sequence variants (ASVs), generated via the DADA2 pipeline, were analyzed in the QIIME2 environment and taxonomically assigned using the SILVA database. Statistical analysis incorporated Linear Mixed-Effects Models (LMM) to evaluate alpha diversity metrics. For beta diversity and differential abundance, analyses were strictly tailored to our paired within-tooth design. title: [Harnessing the regenerative potential of the periodontal ligament: Interdisciplinary framework and innovative indications in tooth autotransplantation].
abstract: Introduction: Tooth autotransplantation combines tooth replacement with preservation of a functional periodontal ligament (PDL). The PDL may contribute not only to periodontal healing but also to the regeneration and remodeling of severely compromised dentoalveolar tissues. This biological potential, combined with an interdisciplinary treatment approach, has expanded the indications for autotransplantation beyond its traditional use in cases of trauma and agenesis. Materials And Methods: A case-based clinical approach is presented involving a 45-year-old male with severe anterior maxillary hard- and soft-tissue loss following trauma, multiple regenerative procedures, and failed implant therapy. Treatment was performed by an interdisciplinary team according to an autotransplantation framework adapted to the stage of tooth development. Clinical and radiographic follow-up, including CBCT, was used to evaluate periodontal healing and hard- and soft-tissue development. The case is complemented by a focused literature-based discussion of the biological and technical principles underlying the framework. Results: Following endodontic treatment and orthodontic preparation, two mature premolars were transplanted into the severely deficient maxillary central incisor region. title: Injectable Nanozyme-Polyphenol GelMA Hydrogel for Mitochondrial Immunomodulation and Periodontal Bone Protection: An in vitro and in vivo Study.
abstract: Purpose: Periodontitis involves persistent oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and dysregulated macrophage activation. This study aimed to develop and evaluate an injectable nanozyme-polyphenol GelMA hydrogel (TCM-Gel) for local periodontal therapy. Methods: TCM-Gel was characterized for physicochemical, antioxidant, and catalase-like properties. Its effects on macrophage mitochondrial indices, inflammatory phenotype, and human gingival fibroblast responses were evaluated in vitro using three independent biological replicates. A ligature-induced mouse periodontitis model included healthy control, Ligature + PBS, and Ligature + TCM-Gel groups (n = 5 mice per group), and local tissue response was assessed in 3 mice. title: Frequent snacking, caries risk, and preventive care delivery in US dental school clinics: A BigMouth data repository study.
journal: Journal of the American Dental Association (1939)
abstract: Background: This study examined the associations between frequent snacking, caries risk classification, clinical indicators of caries, and preventive care delivery among adult dental patients. Methods: Data from 9 institutions participating in the BigMouth Dental Data Repository (UTHealth Houston) were reviewed. Adult patients who underwent oral examinations from July 1, 2022, through August 22, 2023, were included. Frequent snacking was defined as frequent or prolonged intake of sugary foods or drinks between meals per the American Dental Association caries risk assessment form, or as more than 3 between-meal snacks per day per the Consortium for Oral Health-Related Informatics questionnaire. Associations were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, gender, race or ethnicity, and examination type. Results: Among 8,067 adult patients with complete dietary questionnaires, 2,429 (30.1%) reported frequent snacking. Frequent snackers were significantly more likely to be classified as high or extreme caries risk than nonfrequent snackers (91.1% vs 81.3%; adjusted odds ratio, 2.39; 95% CI, 2.03 to 2.82; P < .001) and were independently associated with visible heavy plaque, noncavitated lesions, and cavitated lesions (all P < .001). Despite this elevated risk, frequent snackers had significantly lower odds of receiving prophylaxis (adjusted odds ratio, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.74 to 0.92), and nutritional counseling was documented in only 7.8% of encounters. title: Clinical outcomes of composite restorations with or without a glass ionomer liner after selective caries removal to soft dentin: a 36-month randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Objectives: Selective caries removal to soft dentin (SCR-SD) is currently recommended for the management of deep dentine caries lesions in permanent teeth. However, whether a pulp-protective liner is required after SCR-SD remains uncertain. This randomized controlled trial compared the clinical performance and pulp vitality outcomes of composite resin restorations using a universal adhesive with or without a glass ionomer cement (GIC) liner after SCR-SD in deep caries lesions of permanent posterior teeth. Methods: A randomized controlled clinical trial was conducted in 144 deep dentin caries lesions from 98 participants aged 9 to 55 years. After SCR-SD, lesions were randomly allocated to one of two restorative strategies: a universal adhesive applied in selective enamel etching mode (SE) and composite resin without a GIC liner, or a conventional GIC liner followed by the same universal adhesive applied in selective enamel etching mode and composite resin (GIC + SE). Restorations were followed for 30-36 months. The primary outcome was restoration survival, assessed using selected FDI criteria. The secondary outcome was pulp vitality preservation. Survival analyses were performed using Weibull regression models. Results: Of the 144 treated lesions, 117 were evaluated after 30-36 months. title: Automated assessment of pediatric adenoid hypertrophy on lateral cephalograms using a deep learning-based keypoint approach.
abstract: Background: Adenoid hypertrophy (AH) is common in children and causes upper airway obstruction, which frequently forces oral breathing. In this study, we developed a deep learning framework (AH_KNet) to automatically identify AH and assess its severity using lateral cephalograms, with the aim of providing an objective, non-invasive aid for screening and referral in routine practice. Methods: A cohort of 1,499 lateral cephalograms (899 normal, 600 AH) was collected and divided into training (n = 1,337) and test (n = 162) datasets. A validation subset (n = 162) was randomly extracted from the training set for hyperparameter tuning and internal evaluation. We used a ResNet-50 backbone with a Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) to regress anatomical landmarks and calculate the Adenoidal/Nasopharyngeal (A/N) ratio. To improve robustness, landmark optimization strategy (Method B) was implemented by excluding the unstable Articulare (Ar) point. Results: The proposed approach AH_KNet achieved high reliability in landmark detection (peak ICC = 0.991).
